_readme: Source projects for `python -m hermesbench.supply`, which mutates working code into tasks whose
answer is known by construction and whose verifier already exists. Copy this file, point it at
real checkouts, and drop the `_readme` keys.
python -m hermesbench.supply --manifest <this> --out var/tasks/mut-1 \
--workspace var/mut-ws --report var/mut-1-report.json
WHAT THIS SUPPLY IS AND IS NOT. Mutation tasks carry no withheld check and no commitment, so
`overfit_rate` is undefined for them and they CANNOT become competition challenges. They are
training and benchmark supply. Challenges come from `hermes.taskgen`, which generates both
halves of the verifier.
THEY ARE ALSO THE EASIEST TASK CLASS MEASURED. Published solve rates for procedurally mutated
code run around 65%, against ~41% for bugs that arose naturally from feature work. Use this for
volume; do not expect it to produce tasks the pinned model fails.
LINEAGE, NOT TASK, IS THE SPLIT UNIT. Every mutant of one file shares a lineage and the whole
lineage is drawn into one split. Fewer lineages than splits leaves a split empty and the run
says so. Aim for many target files across many projects, not many mutants of one file.
name          a stable slug; it prefixes every task id generated from this project.
project_dir   relative to THIS manifest, or absolute. The whole directory is embedded into
each task's setup script, minus the excluded dirs in mutation.EXCLUDED_DIRS
(.git, caches, node_modules, .venv) and minus any file that is not UTF-8 text.
Skipped binaries are recorded in the task's metadata.skipped_binary_files --
read that, because a suite that needs a binary fixture cannot be rebuilt here.
target_files  the files to mutate. One lineage per file.
verify        MUST PASS on the unmutated project or the run refuses. MUST NOT rely on a bare
`python`: the harness does not guarantee one on PATH, and the first attempt at
this manifest died on exactly that. Resolve an interpreter explicitly.
protected_paths  the test files. Without them an agent can edit the tests until they pass;
`runner.py` skips the integrity comparison entirely when this is empty.
limit_per_file   optional cap on mutants per file, to keep one large file from dominating.
projects.name: example-ledger
